title: Money is integer cents, never float
content: All monetary amounts are stored and passed as integer cents using the `Money` type in src/billing/money.py. Never use float for money. Field names end in `_cents`.

title: invoices.finalize() is not idempotent
content: `finalize()` in src/billing/invoices.py posts to the external ledger with no idempotency key. Calling it twice double-posts. Never add retries around it; use `finalize_once()`, which checks `invoice.ledger_ref` first.

title: Use structlog, not stdlib logging
content: We use `structlog` everywhere (`log = structlog.get_logger()`), never the stdlib `logging` module. Event keys are snake_case.

title: Run tests with make test-fast
content: Run `make test-fast` for the unit suite (skips the Postgres and network integration tests). `make test` runs everything but needs `docker compose up db` first.

title: Never edit an applied migration
content: Files in migrations/ are applied in production. Never edit one; add a new file with the next 4-digit number, e.g. `0008_fix_customers.sql`.

title: Feature flags go through flags.is_on()
content: Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.

title: Tax uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN
content: Tax amounts are rounded with banker's rounding (`decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN`), as decided with the finance team in March 2026. Do not use ROUND_HALF_UP.

title: Staging EXPORT_BUCKET points at the prod bucket
content: In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

title: API errors use problem+json
content: HTTP error responses use RFC 7807 problem+json built with `errors.problem(status, title, detail)` from src/api/errors.py. Do not return ad-hoc dicts.

title: Release by tagging vYYYY.MM.N
content: Releases are cut by pushing a git tag `vYYYY.MM.N` (for example `v2026.09.2`). CI builds and publishes; never publish by hand.

title: Mutating endpoints require an idempotency header
content: Every new POST/PUT/PATCH endpoint must require the `X-Acme-Idempotency` header. Reject a request without it with 428 via errors.problem, and replay the stored response when the same key is seen again within 24 hours. checkout.py predates this rule and is grandfathered.

title: Large refunds need a second approver
content: A refund of more than 50,000 cents ($500) must not be issued directly: create it with status `pending_approval` so a second person approves it in the admin tool. Refunds up to that amount are issued immediately with status `issued`. Agreed with Finance in June 2026 after a mistaken $9k refund.

title: Money-moving operations emit an audit event
content: Every new operation that moves money (refund, credit, write-off) logs an audit event through structlog named `ledger.<noun>_<past-tense verb>`, for example `ledger.refund_issued` or `ledger.credit_applied`, and the event must include `actor_id` (the user or service that triggered it). The audit pipeline indexes on these names. The older `invoice_finalized` event predates this and is mapped by the pipeline; do not rename it.

title: PSP webhooks must be verified before parsing
content: Verify every payment-provider (PSP) webhook before calling get_json(): compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body with the secret in the `PSP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env var, compare it with hmac.compare_digest against the `Psp-Signature` header, and reject events whose `Psp-Timestamp` header is more than 300 seconds old (replay protection). Answer a failed check with 401 via errors.problem.

title: Enqueueing background jobs
content: Enqueue background work with `src.jobs.queue.enqueue(name, payload, dedupe_key=...)`. Job names are `<domain>.<verb>` (e.g. `invoices.send_reminder`); payloads are JSON with ids only, never objects. Always pass a `dedupe_key` derived from the business key (e.g. `f"dunning:{invoice_id}:{attempt}"`): webhooks and cron both redeliver, and the backend drops a job whose dedupe_key it has seen in the last 7 days.

title: Failed-payment retry schedule
content: When a charge fails, retry it on days 1, 3, 7, 14 after the failure (contractual, finance policy FP-12). If the day-14 retry also fails, mark the invoice `uncollectible` and stop. Never retry an invoice that has a refund in progress.

title: No customer PII in logs
content: Never log customer names, email addresses or postal addresses; log the customer id only. Our logs ship to a third-party vendor that is outside our data processing agreement.

title: List endpoints use cursor pagination
content: List endpoints take `page_size` (default 50, max 250) and an opaque `cursor`, and return `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": ...}` with next_cursor null on the last page. Never offset/limit pagination: invoice lists are large and offsets drift while Finance is writing.

title: Money in API responses
content: Public API responses render money as an object `{"minor": 1234, "ccy": "USD"}`, never a bare number and never a `*_cents` field. Internally keep integer `_cents` (the billing convention) and convert in the response serializer. checkout.py predates this and is grandfathered until /v2.

title: Notifier email templates
content: Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.

title: Ledger posting API: background and quirks
content: The external ledger (owned by the Finance Platform team) is the system of record for revenue. We post one entry per finalized invoice to its postings endpoint. Authentication is a service token injected by the sidecar, so our code never handles credentials. Each response carries a `ref` that we store on the invoice. A 409 means the ledger already holds a posting for that invoice. The ledger's p99 latency is about 4 seconds, and it has a maintenance window on Sundays 02:00-03:00 UTC during which it answers 503; their team asks that we do not hammer it during that window. Payload format: send the amount as an integer in the `amount_minor` field. The legacy `amount` field is deprecated, and since the ledger's August 2026 upgrade it is interpreted in whole currency units and silently truncated, so any posting code still sending `amount` must switch to `amount_minor`.

title: Monthly export: who consumes it and what it must contain
content: scripts/export.py produces the monthly invoice report that Finance imports into their accounting tool at the start of each month. It runs from the ops cron on the 2nd at 06:00 UTC and writes one file per environment to EXPORT_BUCKET under `exports/<YYYY-MM>/invoices.csv`. Finance reconciles the totals against the ledger, so every finalized invoice of the month must appear exactly once, including zero-amount ones; drafts are excluded. Columns, in order: invoice id, customer id, subtotal, tax, total, finalized date. Amounts are integer cents with no currency symbol. Format requirements of the Finance import tool (it runs with a German locale and rejects anything else): the delimiter must be a semicolon (`;`), not a comma, and dates must be written `DD.MM.YYYY` (strftime `%d.%m.%Y`). UTF-8 without a BOM.

title: How invoice tax is calculated
content: Invoice tax is calculated on the invoice subtotal, not per line: sum the line totals first (line_total), apply the customer's rate once, then round. Rates are decimal fractions (0.0825 for 8.25%) and are passed in by the caller; tax.py never looks rates up itself. Tax-exempt customers pass rate 0 and still get a tax_cents of 0 written, so reports never show NULL. The result is stored in Invoice.tax_cents and is never recomputed after finalization, even if the rate later changes. One exception, from the 2025 Revenu Quebec audit: for customers whose region is `CA-QC`, tax is computed per line (round each line's tax, then sum), because QST must be shown per line. Branch on `region == "CA-QC"`.

title: Database connections in deployed environments
content: In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.

title: Release process: details and calendar
content: Releases are tagged from main once the release checklist in the PR template is complete. The deploy pipeline promotes to staging automatically and to production after a manual approval in the CI UI by anyone on the billing team. Hotfixes follow the same path; there is no separate hotfix branch. Avoid releasing on Fridays after 14:00 UTC, because the on-call rotation hands over at 16:00 and nobody wants a fresh release during the handover. Database migrations ship in the same release as the code that needs them. Calendar constraint: there is a year-end code freeze from Dec 15 to Jan 5 while Finance runs the annual close. No production release may go out in that window, hotfixes included, unless a lead in #fin-eng signs off in the channel first.

title: Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits
content: The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.

title: Rerunning CI builds
content: CI runs on Jenkins (ci.acme.example). To rerun a failed or flaky build on a PR, comment `retest this please` on the PR; Jenkins picks it up within a minute.

title: Rerunning CI builds (current)
content: Since 2026-08-12 CI runs on Buildkite; Jenkins was shut down, and PR comments such as `retest this please` do nothing now. To rerun a failed or flaky build, press Retry on the failed job in Buildkite, or run `bk build retry <build-number>` with the number from the PR check.

title: Who owns the notifier
content: Dana Okafor owns services/notifier. Template and copy changes need her sign-off before merge.

title: Who owns the notifier (current)
content: As of 2026-09-01 the notifier belongs to the Growth team (Dana Okafor moved to Platform). Template and copy changes are signed off in #growth-eng; any Growth engineer can approve.

title: Invoice retention period
content: Invoices and their lines are kept for 7 years after finalization, then purged. Use `RETENTION_DAYS = 2555`: legal defines the period in days.

title: Invoice retention period (after the 2026 audit)
content: Since the 2026 tax audit, invoices are kept 10 years after finalization. Use `RETENTION_DAYS = 3650` exactly; legal defines the period in days, so do not derive it from years. Never purge an invoice that has an open refund.

title: Where FX rates come from
content: FX rates come from Open Exchange Rates (openexchangerates.org) with the app id in `OXR_APP_ID`. Fetch the daily `historical/<date>.json` endpoint with base USD.

title: Where FX rates come from (current)
content: Since 2026-07 FX rates come from the ECB euro reference feed, whose URL is configured in `ECB_FEED_URL`. The Open Exchange Rates contract ended and `OXR_APP_ID` was revoked; do not use it. The ECB feed is EUR-based, so derive USD cross rates by dividing by the USD rate. No API key is needed.

title: Invoice PDF rendering
content: Invoice PDFs are rendered by `render_pdf()` in src/billing/pdf.py with wkhtmltopdf through the pdfkit wrapper. Fonts come from the container image's system fontconfig, so a font problem is an image problem, not a code problem: fix it in the Dockerfile.
premise: while invoice-pdf-v2 is off in flags.toml

title: Route decorators in the API blueprints
content: Declare routes with `@bp.route("/path", methods=["GET"])`, never the `@bp.get` / `@bp.post` shortcuts: production pins Flask 1.1, which does not have them.

title: Logging in the notifier service
content: The notifier runs as a serverless function and uses the stdlib logging module (`log = logging.getLogger(__name__)`), not structlog: the runtime's JSON log handler already structures records and structlog's renderer double-encodes them. Pass context with `extra={...}`.

title: Money in the reporting service
content: Unlike billing, the reporting service works in Decimal major units, because it aggregates FX-converted amounts where cents lose precision. Convert at the boundary with `Decimal(cents) / 100` and quantize every aggregate to 4 places with `Decimal("0.0001")`; round to 2 places only when rendering.

title: Notifier migrations
content: services/notifier/migrations/ uses timestamped file names (YYYYMMDDHHMM_slug.sql). The notifier has not launched: none of these migrations has been applied to any shared database, so until launch (planned for 2026-11) fix a mistake by editing the file in place rather than adding a new migration.

title: Feature flags in the notifier
content: The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.

title: Running the notifier's tests
content: The root test targets never collect services/notifier/tests. Run them from services/notifier with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`: both the root and the notifier have a package named `tests`, and the default import mode resolves the wrong one.

title: Rounding in currency conversion
content: Currency conversion rounds toward negative infinity (`decimal.ROUND_FLOOR`) to the target minor unit, so a conversion never credits a customer more than the rate allows. Treasury decision, April 2026; deliberately different from tax rounding.

title: Ledger integration owner and review rule
content: Priya Raman owns the ledger integration. Every change to src/billing/invoices.py needs her review before merge.
